cohort: One hundred pregnant women aged 20-42 years in their second and third trimesters undergoing routine antenatal visits were included, excluding those with a history of Caesarian section, uterine fibroids, or multiple gestation.
finding: Anterior placentation was the most common site (44%), followed by posterior (30%), fundal (20%), and placenta previa (3%), with no statistically significant association found between placental localization and maternal age, gestational age, fetal weight, gender, fetal presentation, or fetal heart rate.
